Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

see to it that verb

also see that you do it, make sure that, I’ll see to it that, take care that

classical

Cic. Att. 3.7.3: vidēre tē cupiō. cūrā ut valeās.
Traupman 107: I’ll see to it that …, cūrābō ut (+ subj.)

cūrā ut (+ subj.)

imperative of cūrāre with ut and the subjunctive; future cūrābō ut, I’ll see to it that

see to it that, take care that

The letter-writer’s cūrā ut valeās is “look after yourself”: literally “see to it that you are well”.

Other words

  • facitō ut (+ subj.) — see that you …, mind you …

    future imperative of facere with ut (utī) and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cato Agr. 5.6: arātra vōmerēsque facitō utī bonōs habeās; Plaut. Mil. 4.4.1: praecepta facitō ut meminerīs (Lewis & Short s.v. meminī); Traupman 107: see that you do it, facitō ut faciās

    The future imperative gives a standing instruction: Cato’s farm manual is full of facitō.

Examples

  • cūrā ut valeās et nōs amēs et tibi persuādeās tē ā mē frāternē amārī

    look after yourself, love us, and be sure that I love you like a brotherCic. Att. 1.5.8

  • Facitō ut faciās.

    See that you do it.Traupman 107
